headline: Energy Leads a Split Session as Month-End Selling Clips Consumer and Healthcare
body_html:
Friday's session closed out July on a cautious note, with advancers edging decliners 273 to 246 across the 519-stock universe — a narrow majority that masked sharper divergences beneath the surface. Energy was the clear pole position, adding 1.64%, while Software gained 0.89% and Industrials tacked on 0.71%. The commodity and enterprise-software cohorts attracted the bulk of fresh money as institutions squared month-end books.

The other side of the ledger was less forgiving. Homebuilders shed 1.72%, Healthcare dropped 0.97%, and Consumer names fell 0.89% — a rotation pattern consistent with defensive repositioning heading into August. Materials finished fractionally in the red, underscoring broad uncertainty about the demand outlook even as energy prices held firm.

The session's most dramatic single-stock move belonged to DexCom, which surged nearly 12% to claim top-gainer honors — a striking outcome inside a healthcare sector that otherwise struggled. Roblox, meanwhile, cratered 26.85%, the steepest loss in the universe, signaling that investor patience with high-multiple, slower-growth consumer internet names has worn thin as the summer stretch run begins.

briefs.headline: DexCom's Double-Digit Surge Stands Apart in a Weak Healthcare Tape
briefs.body: DexCom jumped 11.95% on Friday, bucking a broader healthcare sector decline of nearly 1%. The glucose-monitoring specialist's outperformance suggests company-specific catalysts — likely earnings or guidance — overrode the sector headwind. It was the largest single-day gain in the entire universe tracked by this desk.

briefs.headline: Roblox Suffers Its Sharpest Drop in Recent Memory, Falling Nearly 27%
briefs.body: Shares of Roblox collapsed 26.85% Friday in the session's most punishing individual move. The gaming-platform operator has faced mounting scrutiny over its monetization trajectory, and Friday's selloff suggests quarterly results or forward guidance badly missed investor expectations heading into the back half of 2026.

briefs.headline: Amazon CEO Moves to Calm AI Spending Anxiety
briefs.body: Amazon's chief executive offered a pointed defense of the company's accelerating artificial-intelligence capital outlays, addressing investor concern that the build-out is outpacing near-term returns. His remarks appeared to resonate broadly with technology investors, reinforcing the session's positive tone in the Software segment.

briefs.headline: Microsoft's Rally Prompts Options Strategists to Weigh Alternative Entry Points
briefs.body: Microsoft shares extended a strong run Friday, pushing some market strategists to outline derivative-based approaches for investors who feel they have missed the primary move. The dynamic illustrates how stretched valuations in large-cap software are reshaping how sophisticated investors gain exposure.

briefs.headline: MasTec Plunges 18.91% as Infrastructure Enthusiasm Meets Earnings Reality
briefs.body: Construction and infrastructure contractor MasTec fell nearly 19% Friday, one of the worst prints in the Industrials space despite the sector's overall 0.71% gain. The sharp divergence signals that earnings execution — not just sector tailwinds — is what the market is rewarding or punishing in the current environment.

briefs.headline: Prediction-Market Operator Kalshi Faces Legal Challenge from New York State
briefs.body: New York's attorney general filed suit against prediction-market platform Kalshi, alleging the company is operating an unlicensed gambling enterprise within the state. The action adds regulatory cloud to a fast-growing corner of fintech and could have implications for the broader event-contracts industry as it seeks mainstream legitimacy.
